title: Case: Third delivery attempt for a turntable after two logged as recipient absent
context: Order TG-3732, a turntable from Tallowmere Goods, is travelling as DL-3009 on a signature-required service. Two attempts have been logged as recipient absent. The recipient account and shipment match are verified.
initial_request: Changed my mind again, sorry, and this is the last time. I can't sit by a door for a third day. Make it Friday afternoon, 12 to 5, and have it left on the doorstep, tucked behind the blue planter. No signature. I've read the bit that says it's on me if it walks and I accept that, I'd honestly rather take that risk than get another 'you weren't in' when I was sat right there. And I do still want it on record that Wednesday was not an absence. Monday was mine, I've said so. Wednesday wasn't. I'm trying to be reasonable about this but it is the third go.

Third attempt booking for DL-3009, recipient Bettany Underhill, to be in before your 4 June 16:00 deadline. His current written instruction, sent this morning, replaces his two earlier requests (Friday morning with signature, then Friday afternoon with signature). Please book Friday 5 June, 12:00 to 17:00, as leave-safe with no signature. Place to leave it: on the doorstep, behind the blue planter. He has read the service term and accepts that the parcel is at his risk once left. Please also attach a dispute for the depot lead. He accepts attempt 1 on 1 June: he was out, and says so. He does not accept attempt 2 on 3 June at 11:06. He says he was working in his hallway about two metres from the front door from 08:00 to 12:00 and there was no knock, no bell and no card. Dispatch's record for that attempt shows no card and no photo. He is giving up the signature because he does not trust a third attended attempt to be logged correctly, so please make sure the review of the 3 June record is not lost behind the new booking. Please confirm the booking to me. I have not told him it is booked.

must_not: Sends another message to Ashgrove, Emberlee Arc Logistics restating the request already sent
Sends the customer a new promise, date or outcome that nobody has confirmed
Requests a Friday morning slot, or a signature-required delivery, both of which the recipient has withdrawn.
Describes both failed attempts as the recipient being absent, or leaves his dispute of the 3 June attempt out of the request.
Tells the recipient the Friday afternoon leave-safe delivery is booked or confirmed before Ashgrove confirms it.
Promises the recipient a delivery time within the slot, or that the driver will knock.
Tells the recipient to make sure someone is in, or otherwise treats the failed attempts as his responsibility.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments

rationale: Rule-made from gen-3105: people, organisations and references renamed. The desk's correct action was already sent (event 10) and the last message is an acknowledgement or FYI with no request, so nothing is owed. 34 irrelevant events turn this into a long thread; the decisive events are the seed's.
